business: Schleswig Bike Share (working name): app-based bike sharing, 10-bike pilot
target: Young people aged 14 to 25 living in or around Schleswig, Germany, who need to get around town without a car

segments.name: School pupil (money is pocket money or a small side job; amounts are in euros)
Apprentice or vocational student (amounts are in euros)
University student or volunteer-year participant (amounts are in euros)
Young worker in their first job (amounts are in euros)

behaviours.name: Owns a bike already
behaviours.how: Rides their own bike for most trips and only thinks about alternatives when it is broken or stolen.

behaviours.name: Bus and lifts
behaviours.how: Takes the bus or gets driven by parents or friends; plans trips around the timetable.

behaviours.name: Walker
behaviours.how: Walks most places because the town is small; rarely pays to get around.

behaviours.name: Tight budget
behaviours.how: Counts every euro, needs parents' OK for subscriptions, cancels anything not used weekly.

behaviours.name: Trend and app user
behaviours.how: Tries new apps early, has used e-scooters or bike shares in bigger cities.

behaviours.name: Train commuter
behaviours.how: Travels by train to school, training or work and needs to cover the last stretch.

objections: I already have my own bike
With only 10 bikes, there won't be one near me when I need it
12 € a month is too much for how little I'd use it
My parents would have to set up the payment
What if the bike is broken or the lock doesn't open?
The town is so small I can just walk
In winter and rain I won't ride anyway
habits: you live in a village outside town and depend on the bus
your school is a 20-minute walk from home
you go to sports training twice a week in the evening
you meet friends in the old town on weekends
you arrive at the train station most mornings
your own bike has a flat tyre you have not fixed
